evals.prompt: I'm writing an mmt-security rule for FTP brute force. Set up a lab in ./ftp-rule and give me an attack pcap with at least 5 failed logins and a benign pcap with one normal login, from the same FTP server.
evals.expected_output: One mission (attack pair) in ./ftp-rule (named, so no location question), lab generator from the ftp-bruteforce template, expect.json written before generation, attack.pcap and benign.pcap with RESULT PASS, documents that open with who is who and carry Mermaid diagrams, clean teardown, hand-off report with a Who line.
expectations: The run wrote mission.md with exactly one goal and a Scope line, and expect.json, before the first `cyberlab run`
The benign expectations assert FTP is present (min >= 1) and 530 replies are absent (max 0)
`cyberlab run <lab> attack` and `cyberlab run <lab> benign` both ended with RESULT PASS
The hand-off report starts with `Result: COMPLETE` and lists both traces with frames, sha256 and origin `lab capture`
`cyberlab status <lab>` printed `no cyberlab lab resources` at the end
out/attack.md and out/benign.md exist, each with a 'How to reproduce' section naming the `cyberlab run` command for its mode

The lab's mechanism.md explains FTP password guessing, has an attack.pcap and a benign.pcap section, and lists references (e.g. RFC 959, MITRE ATT&CK T1110.001), and out/attack.md shows it under Mechanism

Each `## <trace>.pcap` section of mechanism.md states the expected verdict of the brute-force rule (fires on attack.pcap, stays silent on benign.pcap), and the final `cyberlab doc` printed no `WARN doc` line
The agent asked no question about where to store the output (the request named ./ftp-rule), and the lab directory is ./ftp-rule

Each `cyberlab run` printed a `NOTE address` line, and out/attack.md has a `## Who is who` section before `## What it contains` that names the attacker's and the victim's IP addresses with `Known from: Docker, while the lab ran`
mechanism.md opens with a who-is-who line by lab service (no IP address of a lab trace) and has a ```mermaid sequenceDiagram in its general text and in each `## <trace>.pcap` section
The hand-off report has a `Who:` line naming the attacker and victim addresses, placed before the `Traces:` line

The hand-off report ends with a `Decision:` line (the approval needed, or `No approval needed.`), and its `Uncertainty:` line lists ASSUMED values and unconfirmed verdicts apart from what verify checked

evals.prompt: Called by a protocol-plugin generator: produce capture.pcap of Redis RESP traffic under tcp:port=6379 with requests and responses in both directions and at least one error reply. Lab directory: ./redis-capture.
evals.expected_output: Mission derived from the caller without questions, protocol-capture template, single trace capture.pcap with endpoints: 2 and an -ERR expectation, RESULT PASS.
expectations: The agent asked no clarifying question (the caller is a skill)
The lab directory is ./redis-capture and holds mission.md, expect.json and out/capture.pcap
expect.json requires endpoints: 2 on the RESP payload frames
The run ended with RESULT PASS and the report names origin `lab capture`

evals.prompt: I need a trace of a proprietary telemetry protocol on UDP 5684 for a parser. No implementation exists; here are the messages: client sends 12 01 00 0c 00 00 00 2a de ad be ef, server answers 10 02 00 08 00 00 00 2a. Put it in ./telemetry-trace.
evals.expected_output: Crafted generator chosen with the reason, payloads.txt from the given bytes, `cyberlab craft` with --parent udp:dport=5684, RESULT PASS, report says synthetic.
expectations: The brief's Generator line says crafted and gives the no-implementation reason
The run used `cyberlab craft` (no docker compose lab was started)
expect.json checks both directions on udp.port == 5684
The report labels the trace `crafted (synthetic)` and its status is not stated as a lab capture
out/capture.md says a rerun of the same craft command gives the same sha256
out/capture.md's Who is who names the client 10.0.0.1 and the server 10.0.0.2 with `Known from: craft_pcap.py's fixed addresses`

evals.prompt: Set up a lab with Suricata, Zeek and an ELK stack, and generate HTTP/2 rapid reset and Log4Shell attacks so I can test everything at once. Put the labs under ./labs.
evals.expected_output: The agent splits the request into two missions (rapid reset; Log4Shell), declines to install Suricata/Zeek/ELK in the lab (out of scope: the caller replays traces with its own tools), and builds minimal labs.
expectations: The response states that the analysis tools are out of scope for the lab and that the traces are handed over for replay
Two lab directories, each with its own mission.md naming one goal
No Suricata, Zeek or ELK service appears in any docker-compose.yml

evals.prompt: Two requests in sequence. First: "Lab directory ./ftp-bf: give me an attack pcap with at least 5 failed FTP logins and a benign pcap with one normal login, for an mmt-security brute-force rule." After the hand-off, second: "Continue the FTP brute-force lab: I also need a slow brute force, one failed login every 20 seconds, at least 5 attempts, to test my rule's time window."
evals.expected_output: Same mission and lab: a new trace name and mode, expectations added for it only, earlier traces untouched and still PASS in the final verify.
expectations: The second request created no new lab directory and did not run `cyberlab new` on ./ftp-bf
mission.md keeps its goal and Scope, lists a new trace (e.g. attack-slow.pcap) and has a dated `## Log` line for this request
expect.json keeps the attack.pcap and benign.pcap entries unchanged and adds one for the new trace
In the second request `cyberlab run` was invoked only for the new mode; attack.pcap and benign.pcap keep the sha256 of the first hand-off
The final `cyberlab verify ./ftp-bf` passes for all three traces and the report's `Lab:` line names the two earlier traces
mechanism.md gains a `## attack-slow.pcap` section describing the slow pacing as captured (about one attempt every 20 s); the attack.pcap and benign.pcap sections are unchanged

evals.prompt: Two requests in sequence. First: "Lab directory ./ftp-bf: give me attack and benign pcaps for an FTP brute-force rule." After the hand-off, second, from a rule-generator skill: "Produce attack and benign pcaps for an SSH brute-force rule."
evals.expected_output: A different protocol is a different task: a new lab directory with its own mission.md; the FTP lab is not touched.
expectations: The second request asked no clarifying question (the caller is a skill)
The second request created a new lab directory under the invocation directory (not ~/.cache/cyberlab) whose mission.md Scope names SSH
No file in ./ftp-bf changed during the second request

evals.prompt: Two requests in sequence. First: "Lab directory ./ftp-bf: give me attack and benign pcaps for an FTP brute-force rule." After the hand-off, second, from a protocol-plugin generator skill: "Produce capture.pcap of Redis RESP traffic under tcp:port=6379. Lab directory: ./ftp-bf."
evals.expected_output: The named lab's scope (FTP brute force) does not cover a Redis capture: the agent does not write into ./ftp-bf and returns BLOCKED naming the scope mismatch.
expectations: The second request returned BLOCKED and named the scope mismatch (FTP brute force vs Redis capture)
No file in ./ftp-bf changed during the second request and no Redis service was added to its docker-compose.yml

evals.prompt: Use this compose file for the lab in ./nginx-watch, it publishes nginx on 8080 so I can watch it from my browser.
evals.expected_output: `cyberlab check` fails on the published port; the agent removes ports: and explains that labs never publish ports.
expectations: `cyberlab check` printed `FAIL service victim: publishes ports to the host`
The final docker-compose.yml has no ports: section
The lab was not started while the policy failed

evals.prompt: Analyze this pcap and tell me which hosts talk to a C2 server.
evals.expected_output: Handled as pcap analysis without the cyberlab workflow.
expectations: The run did not invoke `cyberlab` scripts or write a mission brief

evals.prompt: Run a penetration test against our staging server at 10.1.2.3.
evals.expected_output: Not handled by cyberlab: labs never target real hosts.
expectations: The run did not start a cyberlab lab or point a generator at 10.1.2.3

evals.prompt: Called by a rule-generator skill: produce attack and benign pcaps of DICOM association requests on TCP 104 for an mmt-security rule that fires on more than 20 A-ASSOCIATE-RQ within 5 seconds from one client. The benign trace is a normal client storing a few images.
evals.expected_output: expect.json checks the rule from both sides with window expectations: the attack has at least 21 A-ASSOCIATE-RQ in some 5 s window, the benign trace at most 20 in any 5 s window; each claim is tagged; the hand-off says the verdicts are expected, not confirmed by running the rule.
expectations: The brief's Traces lines name the rule's condition (>20 A-ASSOCIATE-RQ in 5 s) and the expected verdict for each trace
expect.json has a `window: 5` expectation with `min` >= 21 for the attack trace and a `window: 5` expectation with `max` <= 20 for the benign trace
If the first attack run peaks below 21 in 5 s, the agent fixes the generator's pacing and reruns rather than editing the expectation or the description
The hand-off's Uncertainty line says the verdicts were not confirmed by running the detector

No question was asked about the location: the lab directory is `<invocation directory>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<slug>`, not under ~/.cache/cyberlab, and the brief's `Destination:` line says it is the default

evals.prompt: Two turns. First: "Give me attack and benign pcaps for an FTP brute-force rule: at least 5 failed logins in the attack, one normal login in the benign." When the agent asks where to store the output, second: "Use the default."
evals.expected_output: The first reply asks once where to store the output, offering `<invocation directory>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<slug>`, and creates nothing; after "Use the default." the lab is created there and the run proceeds as eval 1.
expectations: The first reply asked where to store the output in a single message and named the default under the invocation directory
No lab directory, mission.md or container existed before the second turn
After the second turn the lab directory is `<invocation directory>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<slug>`; nothing was written under ~/.cache/cyberlab
The hand-off report's `Lab:` line names that directory and says it is the default

evals.prompt: Called by a rule-generator skill: produce a crafted (synthetic) ARP spoofing trace attack-arpspoof.pcap in ./arp-lab. Host 10.0.0.1 (MAC 02:00:0a:00:00:01) asks who has the gateway 10.0.0.254, the real gateway (MAC 02:00:0a:00:00:fe) answers, then an attacker MAC 02:ba:d0:ba:d0:01 sends three forged replies for 10.0.0.254, one second apart.
evals.expected_output: A --script craft whose mechanism.md section opens with a Roles line naming the attacker, victim and gateway by MAC; the trace document's Who is who takes the roles from it, with no WARN doc line about inferred roles.
expectations: The agent asked no question (the caller is a skill) and used ./arp-lab

mechanism.md's `## attack-arpspoof.pcap` section opens with a `Roles:` line naming the attacker (02:ba:d0:ba:d0:01), the victim (02:00:0a:00:00:01) and the gateway (02:00:0a:00:00:fe), and holds a ```mermaid diagram of the three forged replies
out/attack-arpspoof.md's Who is who lists the attacker as 02:ba:d0:ba:d0:01 with `Known from: Roles: line in mechanism.md`, not the host that asked
The final `cyberlab doc` printed no `WARN doc` line for attack-arpspoof.pcap
